/-!
# Erdős Problem 303

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/303](https://www.erdosproblems.com/303)
- [BrRo91] Brown, Tom C. and Rödl, Voijtech, Monochromatic solutions to equations with unit
  fractions. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1991), 387-392.
-/

namespace Erdos303

/--
Is it true that in any finite colouring of the integers there exists a monochromatic solution
to $\frac 1 a = \frac 1 b + \frac 1 c$ with distinct $a, b, c$?

This is true, as proved by Brown and Rödl [BrRo91].

This was formalized in Lean by Yuan using Seed-Prover.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/303"]
theorem erdos_303 :
    answer(True) ↔
    -- For any finite colouring of the integers
    ∀ (𝓒 : ℤ → ℤ), (Set.range 𝓒).Finite →
      -- There exists integers `a, b, c`
      ∃ (a b c : ℤ),
      -- that are non-zero and distinct.
      [a, b, c, 0].Nodup ∧
      -- `a, b, c` satisfy the equation
      (1/a : ℝ) = 1/b + 1/c ∧
      -- `a, b, c` have the same color
      (𝓒 '' {a, b, c}).Subsingleton := by
  sorry

end Erdos303

reformulations.difference: Brown–Rödl formulate their result for positive integers; the Lean statement permits arbitrary nonzero integer witnesses.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The positive-integer version implies the integer version by restricting a colouring to positive inputs. Conversely, encode a positive-integer colouring c by D(n)=2c(n) for n>0 and D(n)=2c(-n)+1 for n<0, assigning any colour to zero. This still has finite range. A monochromatic nonzero triple for D has a common sign because the two branches have opposite parity. If negative, negate all three entries. This preserves distinctness and the reciprocal equation and produces a positive triple monochromatic for c. Restriction and extension handle the colouring domains. The equivalence between the Lean right-hand side and its positive-witness version was proved independently in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean, without sorryAx.

sources_consulted: Brown, T. C. and Rödl, V., Monochromatic solutions to equations with unit fractions, Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. 43 (1991), 387–392, especially Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.3. Full text: https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/S0004972700029221 (read through r.jina.ai).

review.notes: Checked the sole declaration against the exact source question and Brown–Rödl’s Corollary 2.3, specialized to n=2 and coefficient 1. Finite-range integer labels faithfully represent finite colourings; [a,b,c,0].Nodup imposes precisely distinctness and nonzero denominators; the subsingleton image expresses equal colours. Lean confirms that all three divisions are real-valued. Boundary tests accept the constant-colouring witness (2,3,6) and reject zero or repeated denominators. The affirmative answer, solved category, and formal-proof record match the source. The linked proof has exactly the required conclusion; after scratch-only Lean/Mathlib compatibility updates, it compiled with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound as axioms.
